column2: the writer's notes (doubts; where the article disagrees with the entry): for the data check

Article says EPRDF led 1988-2018 and ends with events up to Sept 2026 (a renewed offensive); left out as unverifiable and recent. Article calls TPLF former ruling party; Prosperity Party merger described as per article. Legal status/terrorist designation omitted.
Article gives birth as c. 1914 and 15 October 1914; entry says 1914. Article is thin (about 400 words); family section on his son and brother left out.

Article gives the rename to VSN as both 'after 1962' and 1970; the entry says 1962, so the year is left out. Article text 'Tontons Macoutes murdered between 30,000 and 60,000' stated as credited figure.

Entry says hundreds of bridges and tunnels; article gives about 230 tunnels and 4100 bridges, so the counts are left out. Entry says Zagros; article names the Alborz only. Article's Persian Corridor claims about removing Reza Shah left out.

Entry gives Armenia ~10,000 km2 and overturning by Mudros Oct 1918; the article gives neither (it says less than one ninth of Eastern Armenia), so both are omitted. The article says the treaty needed confirmation by the Central Powers; omitted.

Article says Silesia was lost in 1748 and also cites the 1742 and 1745 treaties; dates for the cession are left out. Entry mentions Frederick's promise of a vote to Joseph; not in the article, left out.

Entry says the castle was begun by Hugh de Lacy and completed by Walter, and that Trim was seat of a liberty; article only says late 12th century and Hugh de Lacy, so these points are left out. Article calls the earlier burned-castle episode without a date.

Entry gives 81,258 blocks and carving 1236-1251; article gives 81,352 blocks (81,258 pages) and carving from 1237 in 12 years. Block count and start year are left out; 81,258 used as pages as the article does. Article's claim that the Haeinsa depository was UNESCO listed omitted.

Article gives Tibet's Chan mission 'in about 761' for Kim Hwasang and 763 for a second party; used loosely. Article's Tibetan-lost-cities dates (694, 703) belong to earlier reigns. Samye foundation date not given in the article, so none printed (entry says c. 779).
Entry says the dzong is seventeenth-century; article gives 1644. Entry names Ugyen Wangchuck as penlop; article does not, so omitted. The article's Yoeling account is told as a local account.

Article gives Old Style 30 January = 9 February 1667; entry says January 1667. Article says treaty is sometimes called a treaty; entry says Russo-Polish War of 1654-1667 (article: war since 1654). Background section omitted for lack of material; two sections.

Entry says annals record the Assuwa defeat and dates him late 15th or early 14th c. BCE; the article gives c. 1465-c. 1440 BC and mentions no Assuwa or annals (the western campaigns belong to Tudhaliya II). Neither is printed. Heading Death and legacy used because the article only mentions death in the opening; the text mostly covers legacy in scholarship, which is a slight stretch.
Entry frames Turkification as the Seljuk/Manzikert process; the article broadens it to Central Asia, Azerbaijan and Ottoman policy. Heading Reception and legacy used for the late Ottoman period.

Entry says Duke John held court in the 1550s and 1560s; article says only mid-16th century. Article lists the castle as 'most visited museum' with annual numbers; kept the plain claim only; may be a ranking—consider cutting.

Entry says the succession dispute opened the way for the sack of Washukanni; the article says the Hittites failed to capture the capital, so no sack is printed. Article says Tushratta died c. 1335 BC; the entry has no dates. Amenhotep IV (Akhenaten) is called Akhenaten in the entry; the article uses Amenhotep IV.

SKIPPED: the article is about 280 words (size, branches, islands, name, one 2011 event), adds too little to the entry; also calls it a landlocked fjord where the entry says it is a lake and not a fjord

Entry says the law faculty moved to Rennes in 1735, the French Revolution closed it in 1793 and the present university was refounded in 1962; the article gives early 1960s and 1970 for the re-establishments and no 1735 or 1793, so these are left out. The article's student numbers and rankings are omitted.

Entry says plaques show him carrying a basket of earth; article says a basket of bricks, so the contents are given as the article has it only in the relief; consider reconciling. Entry r. c. 2500 BCE; article fl. c. 2520 BC; no date printed. Article's Sumerian king list excerpt ('acted for 1080 years') omitted.

Article is inconsistent about who was president and who vice president in 1833 and 1846 (it says elected 'president and vice president respectively' but also that they shared and alternated); the entry says vice-president and acting president several times. Offices are therefore not assigned. Article does not state that he went into exile in 1834 beyond leaving for New Orleans.
Article has no history of the region; entry's statement about the Duchy of Guelders is not in the article. Recent reintroductions (wolf from 2019, bison) omitted.

Entry gives c. 817-830; article says suggested dates range from about 817 to 833, so no range is printed. Article's claim that Einhard's wife Emma was not Charlemagne's daughter (a 12th-century fabrication) left out.

Entry says Khazars taxed commerce; article source is ibn Khordadbeh's tithe. Article says route functioned concurrently with the Dnieper route. Article's account of Viking slave-trade background (religious rules on enslavement) left out for space.

Article's later cases (Brnovich 2021, Louisiana v. Callais 2026) and its claims about consequences of Shelby left out as contested or too recent to summarise without assessment. Article says signed 'August 6, 1965'; entry says August 1965: consistent.
Article quotes Cosgrave's 'exterminate ten thousand Republicans' remark; left out. Dates of Fine Gael leadership (1934-1944) match entry.

Entry says Wafd 'negotiated' the 1936 treaty; article says Farouk signed it. Text avoids saying who negotiated. Entry says 'dissolved after 1952 revolution'; article: banned January 1953. Entry's 1978 revival not in this article.

Entry lists counts of Sayn, Nassau, Isenburg, Wied; article lists Sayn, Diez, Wied and Laurenburg/Nassau (no Isenburg). Text names only the article's counts and does not use the entry's list. Westerwaldlied's Nazi-era origin left out.

Article's 'Council of Troyes in August 878' — text above wrongly wrote '1878'; fixed in file. Entry says last count appointed by the Frankish king; article says Wilfred was never confirmed by a monarch as Count of Ausona: left out.

Entry says served four Angevin kings; article says five including Young Henry as co-ruler: no count printed. Entry c. 1146, article 1146 or 1147: no birth date printed. New Ross not in the excerpt, not mentioned.

Entry says 'oldest' settlement; article says 'first English settlement in the state' but also treats Ludlow's Dorchester group as first and the Stiles party as 'second group to settle Connecticut'; the article contradicts itself, so no 'first' claim and no sequence of groups is printed.
Entry: Zhili clique one of the strongest of the 1920s; consistent. Article says he was 'betrayed' by Feng Yuxiang implicitly (deserted). Text is under 380 words by design; article is thin.

Entry says around 130 BCE for expelling the Yuezhi; article gives 133-132 BCE and elsewhere 162 BC for the Yuezhi's flight to the Ili Valley, and Zhang Qian's embassy 125/115 BC with different details: text says only 'in the 130s BCE'. Entry says Wusun absorbed Saka; article says population largely Saka; included only implicitly.

Article calls Witzel the source of 'Advaita' credit; text says Witzel but article gives only 'Witzel': first name not in file, fixed below if flagged. Article states Yajnavalkya Smriti 'more authoritative than Manu's' - left out. Entry says teacher of White Yajurveda and source of Shatapatha Brahmana; article says compiler/seer of Shukla Yajurveda.

Entry says Pereslavl-Zalessky from 1212; article gives no year (bequeathed on Vsevolod's deathbed). Article: sent to 'Pereiaslav' in 1200; entry says Alexander Nevsky born at Pereslavl: article says nothing.
Article says Zeng died 'mysteriously' in Hong Xiuquan's former mansion; left out. Entry mentions Self-Strengthening Movement; article does not: not repeated.

Entry's last sentence about the 'Elamite ruler addressed as father' is not in the article and was ignored; article says Hammurabi was an ally, and diplomatic 'father' language is generic. Article says exile lasted fifteen years.

SKIPPED: article has under about 250 words of substance (composition, popularisation, a list of covers); the description already gives the composition Substance beyond the description: official hymn of the CNT by 1936; sung by the Durruti Column leaving Barcelona; Sorozabal's anecdote; later international left repertoire.

Entry gives birth 1875; article says between 1875 and 1880: no birth year printed. Entry says proclaimed 1907-1908; article says February 1908. Article spells the act 'Algericas' (a slip for Algeciras), so the text does not name it. Article calls Abdelaziz his younger brother; not stated.

Article gives 28 years, 1712-1684 BC (Middle Chronology); entry says c. 1711-1684, so no reign dates are printed. Entry says the Sealand campaign shows loss of southern territories; article says only the failed damming. Thin article.

Entry says 1872-1967 and border fixed 1904-1914; article says informal beginnings after 1839, 1874 Ottoman acceptance, and that the Protectorate of Aden ended in January 1963 (Protectorate of South Arabia followed). No start/end dates for the whole protectorate are printed. Entry 'South Yemen independence 1967' not in article beyond NLF taking power.

Article says 'Bede describes him ruling all England south of the Humber' within 15 years; entry 716-757 matches. Article's legend of Alfred III omitted. Entry says 'to be succeeded after a brief struggle by Offa'; article says Offa 'possibly after a brief civil war'. Beornrad spelling varies (Beornred in lead): used Beornrad as in body.
Dodwell/Soter guardian theory omitted as unresolved. Erythraean Sea date 'about 113 BC' and the Samos namesake left out.
Diodorus says he reigned nine years; 338-331 is seven, so left out.
Article says Bolívar 'crowned' Gamarra's wife: unclear, left out. The article's heading about Peru and Ecuador is evidently a slip for Bolivia. Order of 1829 succession unclear in article; left out.
Article gives 35 institutes and later 'over 40' and a population over 100,000 'currently': left out. Skolkovo comparison and revenue figure left out.
Article calls Alaungpaya one of three greatest monarchs of Burma: left out as praise. Administration (Manu Kye dhammathat, military colonies) and Manipur expeditions omitted for length.
Entry says William I and succession 1389; article says William V and 1388: both left out. Article's title says Duke of Lower Bavaria; not repeated.
Article's 'late 20s' age in 343/2 left out. Article is short (about 370 words).
Article's 'quadroon' wording and 'one of the revolutionary quartet' left out. Dessalines' coronation date 6 Oct 1804 left out as not needed.
Year of the letters patent (21 June) not given in article; stated only as the end of the war. Kindergarten not described in article text read; left out.
Article's 1444/1454 Góis date confusion left out; Cape Verde discovery dispute stated only as disputed. Early galley service 1451-52 and later Albania defence omitted for length.

Article credits Amadeus VI with buying the Col de Largentière for 60,000 ecus but dates it to 1388, after his death: contradictory, left out. Article's account of the Nice transfer (negotiated with Grimaldi) differs in wording from the entry's Dedition; both facts not combined.
Article gives conflicting birth day (28 vs 11 February) and start of schooling; left out. Love story with Ilik Sundari omitted.
Dar ol-Fonun: article says instructors arrived after dismissal; entry says it opened 1851: stated neutrally. Executioner's name omitted.
Article's description of the marriage of 'Age of Romanticism' omitted. Entry says she fought in Uruguay; article only gives the marriage in Montevideo.
Article's lead says European powers appointed Francis Stephen in 1735 while body says 1736 swap; year left out.
NDH propaganda campaign, delegate numbers and Sandžak details left out.
Article contradicts itself on St Peter's dates (1506 start, chief architect from 1520, until 1536): left out. Castro not mentioned in article.
Article's lead says Ulloa joined mission at 19 (1735) and the body gives 1736-1744; left as 'at nineteen'. Entry says 'from 1735'.
Entry says Ariarathes II was adopted son; article says nephew: relationship left out. Article calls Ariarathes the founder of the Iranian Ariarathid dynasty; not repeated.
Entry says Bavarians proclaimed him king in 919; article places the Annales entry in 920 and says the election is unproven: date left out. Entry says submission 921; article says 921 campaigns.

Article dates the coronation 884, 885, 886 or 887 and the reign at 4, 5 or 7 years; entry says 884 or 885, so no year is printed. Article also gives the Karasunk battle as 862 and 863; year left out. Prince of princes 862 matches the entry.

Entry says Portugal abandoned Azemmour in 1541 after the Saadi capture of Agadir; the article gives João III's court's economic difficulties as the reason and does not mention Agadir. Both are given without contradiction (the text states only the abandonment in 1541 and the article's reason). Entry says 'Portugal took it in 1513'; the article also says its inhabitants had been tributaries since 1486.

Desc says they 'migrated into the region over several centuries'; article gives 1391 first evidence and 17th-century formation of the culture. Article says the Baggara do not all consider themselves one people.
Entry calls him margrave and count; article uses both. Article spells the abbey Saint-Bertain in one place; Saint-Bertin used.

Entry says river flows about 100 km and that the region was part of Diyar Mudar in the Middle Ages; article gives no length. Entry names Tell Bi'a at the mouth; article lists it near the confluence. 'Discovery and study' heading used for a river although listed for objects; could be changed by editor.
Entry says the Armenians were defeated and resistance continued; article says religious freedom was allowed afterwards. Fine, not contradictory.

Entry says the battle was in north-eastern Anatolia; article says eastern Anatolia, and gives Köse Dağ 80 km north-west of Sivas; region left out. Entry's claim that fragmentation led to the Ottomans is not in the article and is not repeated.

Entry describes massed musketeers behind palisades against Takeda cavalry and says the battle is 'often cited as a turning point'; the article says three-stage shooting is a later invention and that 'Takeda cavalry' is an inappropriate term. Text avoids calling the Takeda cavalry, mentions only the 3-stage claim as later account. Article gives allied total 38,000 vs Takeda 15,000; Nobunaga 30,000 + Ieyasu 8,000.

Article's Ostrogoth dispute: Jordanes says Ostrogoths fought the Huns; some historians reject this. Entry lists Ostrogoths among peoples forming kingdoms, article says Ostrogoths achieved independence; consistent. Hungarian chronicle mention kept brief.

Article names the Second Battle of Puebla in 1863; entry says French took Puebla the following year, consistent. Article is internally muddled in the Background about Veracruz timing; only the broad sequence used.

Entry traces the name to the ancient Bergistani; the article does not mention this, so it is not repeated. Entry says textiles and coal mining developed in the 19th century; article says mining, textiles, forestry etc. grew c. 1900-1960. Population 44,632 in 2019 given as about 44,600.

Entry says 6th century and calls Liudhard a bishop; article calls him chaplain. Article gives c. 565 birth and death in or after 601 (possibly 606). Entry says father was 'of Paris'; article does not. Entry says she 'worshipped at St Martin's'; article says restored for her.

Entry says 'Many were painted under the Uyghur kingdom of Qocho'; article says 'West Uyghur kingdom' for most surviving caves and names Qocho for the Uyghurs converted. Omitted the genetic and ethnic discussion.

Entry says abandonment 'around the turn of the era'; article says a few decades after the Roman conquest: no date given. Entry says Caesar defeated Helvetii 'nearby'; article 26 km south. Article is 'Beuvray' dates 1865-1895 and 1867-1895 in two places; 1867 used. Moved 'Setting' for a place though it is a hillfort.

Article gives diamonds yield as 2,720 kg and, elsewhere, 3,000 kg; entry says about 2,700 kg and 22 million tonnes. Weight of diamonds left out. 'Tens of thousands of miners' (entry) versus up to 50,000 (article). Article is inconsistent on 'Alyrick' name; omitted. Article dates diggers' camp of 50,000 to 1872.

Entry gives joint rule from c. 435, the Treaty of Margus, raids in the early 440s and death c. 445; none of these is in the article, which says reign of eleven years and that the exact manner of death is unknown. Entry says 'probably killed on Attila's orders'; the article only reports Jordanes's speculation. Text states only the article's version. Article is thin; 'eleven years' is not repeated against the entry's dates in a way that conflicts (435 to 445 is ten); left as the article says.

Entry says the yard 'remains one of Hamburg's landmarks'; not in the article, so omitted. Article says the camp provided labour from July 1944 to April 1945; the 'report dated 29 August' taken as 1944 (the year is implied by the subcamp dates, not stated). Entry says aircraft 'through a subsidiary'; article says the Hamburger Flugzeugbau, renamed 1937.

Entry says the church 'disappeared after the Ottoman conquest of 1463'; article says it was formally dismantled in 1461 after the 1459 persecution, and the conquest followed in 1463. Both dates given as the article states. Article dates Batalo's Gospel to 1393 in one place and 1394 in another; 1394 used (manuscript list). Article: 'existed for two centuries'.

Entry says Maratha armies under Baji Rao I extended power into Bundelkhand in the eighteenth century; the article does not mention the Marathas, so it is not repeated. Entry says 'between the Ganges plain and the Vindhya range'; article says situated in the Vindhya Range. Gave only the movement's start and 2011 proposal; omitted claims about poverty.

Entry says governor-general from 1960 and minister of justice 1948-1959 and mentions the Suppression of Communism Act of 1950; the article says governor-general 1959-1961, Deputy PM 1954-59, and does not name the Act. The text gives no year for his appointment as governor-general and does not name the Act. Peak name change omitted.
Article gives death as 302 or 303; entry says 302, so no year printed. Era names left out.
Entry mentions the stele of King Gwanggaeto and tombs around Huanren and Ji'an; article does not, so omitted.
Article numbers the 1846-49 war Second and the 1872-76 war Third, but its intro counts two; I avoided numbering the later wars. Left out the article's background on earlier centralisation.
Entry says founded 1131; article agrees (built 1131-1240).
SKIPPED: article under 250 words of substance (town facts, a banknote, climate, roads); the entry already tells Taksin and the French occupation, which the article does not
Entry's Modu Chanyu 209-174 BCE and the hierarchy of kings are not in the file, omitted. The file's lists of Xiongnu chanyus are empty.
Entry also says 1861 Canning Award on Zanzibar; not in the file, omitted. Dropped the Oudh proclamation controversy and Ellenborough despatch for length.
Entry says Menton and Roquebrune 'broke away in 1848' and that Charles 'sold' claims in 1861; article says rebellions for decades and 'formally ceded', no years, so I gave none.
Entry says 'eldest son'; article says second son after Pepin the Hunchback, so I gave no birth order. Left out the failed Mercian marriage and blockade.

Article gives 2 populations (115,913 and 62,153); I used neither as a headline. Desc says 'gilded hall and great gateway towers'; article does not mention towers. Stated as: 2011 census counted 62,153 (article's demographics section).
Article's 'the following year' for Carbo taken as 112 BCE (the entry's 113 start). Left out Mommsen's description of Celtic weapons.

Article spells BC; converted. Entry's 'around 200 BCE' matches. Article says the Romans' Severus partition without a date; no date given by me. Eunapius's date c. 350 and c. 400 in the article differ; I wrote 'about 350 CE' once. The sentence 'the name no longer has an official use' is my inference; the article says 'first and only official use' was Seleucid.

Article gives his death as 1101 or possibly 1108; I printed no death year. Entry says he extended rule over Raska and Bosnia; article attributes it to the Chronicle of the Priest of Duklja. Left out the Crusaders' 1097 meeting.
Cut the detailed discussion of Trumbic's and Pasic's positions for length.
Desc says Spaniards stripped the gold in 1533; article says ransom gold was mostly collected from it; I used the latter.
Entry says Asiatic Company succeeded in 1732; article says re-founded 1730; I gave no year. Entry gives 1616-1729 as one span; the article describes two companies.
Entry says darughachi in Goryeo were stationed after the 1231 invasion and killed in summer 1232; article agrees. Entry says withdrawn by 1328 in Russia; same.
Entry says 'among the Iranian crown jewels'; consistent.
Entry says 'would remove even Robert if he submitted'; not in the file, omitted. Article gives 51 sealers (intro), 39 names and 19 surviving seals; I gave two.
Article calls Doson 'half-cousin', entry 'cousin'; I gave no kinship. Entry's Demetrian War not in article; omitted.

Article says temple planning began after 334 BC; entry says begun around 300 BCE: omitted start date of the temple. Article says Ionians settled around 1000 BC and finds only late 8th c.; hedged. Entry says 'south of Miletus'; article says only 16 km linear distance, not stated here.
Article lacks Zhongshan/Later Yan history given in the entry; not repeated. Article's text is short (about 500 words).
Article says c. 1517 written, published 1531: consistent with the entry. Gallic sack 387 BC per article.

SKIPPED: article is about the divan/diwan as Islamic government ministries in general (caliphates, Buyids, Seljuks); the Ottoman imperial council of the entry gets one paragraph, so the article is a broader subject than the entry Entry is the Ottoman Divan-i Humayun council; article's Ottoman material is two sentences.

Entry says de Courcy made Downpatrick the centre of the Anglo-Norman lordship; article says the Normans began a motte but abandoned it when he made Carrickfergus capital in 1178: left out. Entry says near south-western shore of Strangford Lough; article does not say, omitted. Entry's 'Dún Lethglaise' name: article attributes this to Cathedral Hill per Flanagan; omitted.

Dating: entry says 11th-12th century; article gives Thompson 1200-1250, Ruggles 12th-14th century, Satterthwaite no later than 1345 (and lead says 11th or 12th): all dates left out. Typo check 'a own' fixed below if flagged.

Entry says independent in the 8th century; article places the break at 763 (papal switch) but de facto independence from 840 and says it ruled 'more than five centuries'; I avoided saying when independence began. Entry says Amalfi and Sorrento broke away in the 9th c.; article: early 9th century. Article's tenth-century capture by Pandulf IV left out as unclear.

Entry says Hugh O'Neill ruled from its castle; article says he burned it in 1602 - not stated. Entry says chief seat 'from the late Middle Ages'; article: castle built in 14th century. Left out ranking about immigrants.
Article headed 'Reign, 1906-1916' but lead says 1907-1916; entry 1907-1916: dates of reign not stated beyond 1916 coup.
Article does not mention coastal Karnataka or Udupi monasteries (in entry); not repeated.
Article does not mention Haile Selassie's restoration in the provided portion (entry does); not repeated. Order in Course of events: July Sudan attack and Aug Somaliland, summarised.
Entry says dominated Golden Horde about 1396-1411 and born 1352; article gives no birth year and says control lost by 1412-13; omitted both ranges. Entry says Vorskla defeat 1399: consistent.

Article inconsistencies: says 6th year of reign at abdication, and 'Hosokawa Emperor'; left out. Article says mother's father's line: entry's 170 years since Uda used by article; not repeated. Wording 'no Fujiwara father's line' follows the article's 'not of Fujiwara descent paternally'.

Entry mentions Xianbei raids under Tanshihuai: not in the article, omitted. Article says Zhi 'eight-year-old' etc. Article: 'sworn by blood' not repeated. Liang Ji's 159 coup and Li Yun execution both dated 159 in article.

Dates: entry c. 1900-1500 BCE; article gives early estimates 1900-1500 and radiocarbon 1750-1500 since 2007; no dates printed. Erligang dates omitted. Entry mentions turquoise workshops: not in article.

Article dates Allen's capture after the 8 Sept 1775 mission; the capture is stated in the lead, not the excerpt detail. Entry says secret talks with British Canada 'with his brothers'; article says negotiations only. Birth 21 Jan 1738 (O.S. 1737) given by article; not printed.

Article wording 'had lied' softened to 'misled' – attributed to the inquiry. Entry says first French thermonuclear test is Canopus; article calls it 'first two-stage thermonuclear test' – used article's wording.

Entry: 'fired after trying to register in 1962': consistent. Entry says Freedom Summer help; article lead says she organized it. Omitted her stance on abortion (article material, not needed). Articles gives life dates Oct 6 1917 / Mar 14 1977.

SKIPPED: article has under about 250 words of substance (founding in 1714, census figures, zardozi, transport lists) and adds almost nothing to the entry Article gives only 1714 founding by Nawab Muhammad Khan Bangash, zardozi craft, 2011 census; no history.

Article says ratified Feb 3 1870 (lead) and certified March 30 1870; entry says ratified 1870: consistent, date of ratification not printed. Article contradicts itself on vote counts in lead for House (144 Republicans vs 144 to 44); used 144 to 44.

Article's lead says war 1833 to 1840; entry says the same. Convention/Embrace of Bergara named in article only as 'Embrace of Bergara', so left out of text. Entry says last Carlist forces defeated 1840; article section 1839-40 does not say so, left out. '1830s' in text is from the article's 'the 1830s' not present; kept as period phrase.
Section 'Organisation and way of life' used for external support and violence, as nearest allowed heading. Article does not mention 1975 independence claim or Alvor Agreement (entry does); left out.

Article says Christian 'possibly' killed in conflict with Tahitians; entry says killed in 1793 in violence between settlers. Text hedges via Adams's conflicting accounts. Article says Tubuai attempt failed due to conflict with natives.

Article gives Burnham as premier 1964-66 and PM 1964-80 (overlapping); text uses premier then 'after independence'. Article lead calls him 'often regarded as a strongman dictator'; attributed only through Prados. Article says 2016 finding of complicity in Rodney's death; text says 'accused'.

Entry calls him an exile and gives the hold as until 1301; article says four years (1297 to 1301 by implication) and that the Guelphs took refuge on the Rock in 1295, so no explicit year given for loss. Article says purchase from 'crown of Aragon' and then 'Queen Yolande of Aragon'; text uses the latter. Article says Rainier 'II' once, treated as slip for Rainier I.

Entry says he held a nominal army command during the war; article says that on mobilisation in 1914 command of the 7th Army passed to Josias von Heeringen and Frederick, for health reasons, could not serve again in the war. Left the war out. Entry says abdication followed a provisional government in Karlsruhe in November 1918; article gives only the revolution.
Entry says Swiss seized the Aargau including Habsburg Castle; article lists the western Aargau, Freiamt and County of Baden but does not name Habsburg Castle.

Article does not mention the Kabul-Kandahar march, the Indian commander-in-chief dates 1885-1893, or the capture of Johannesburg and Pretoria and the annexation (entry does); left out. Article gives field marshal promotion 25 May 1895 and Ireland command 1 Oct 1895 in that order.

Article says Hitler 'proclaimed the Führerprinzip as the law of the Nazi Party as early as July 1921'; text pairs this with the Drexler episode as the article tells it. Entry's 'replaced collective decision-making and elections' is not directly in the article; left aside.

Article gives 1859 junta selection and 1861 popular election; entry says first term 1861-1865; text keeps both. Entry says Catholicism a condition of citizenship; article says candidates and voters. Entry mentions Quito observatory; not in article, omitted.

Article is titled Gallo-Roman culture. Entry says Gallo-Romans were majority under Visigothic, Burgundian and Frankish kingdoms with separate laws; not in article, omitted. Entry says 'by the 5th century mostly Catholic', not in article.
Entry says archbishopric 'moved to the present Uppsala in the 13th century'; article says 1273 to Östra Aros, renamed Uppsala. Article: Celsius buried at Gamla Uppsala Church.
Entry calls Gaochang a kingdom conquered in 640; article agrees. Article gives Qu kingdom 501-640 CE.

Entry says in 1071 his brothers Sancho II and Alfonso VI deposed him; article has Alfonso invading in 1071, Sancho acquiescing, and Sancho defeating García in 1072. Text follows article's sequence without dating the deposition. Birth: article 1041/April 1043, entry 1042; left out.

Entry says around 1000 they came under the kings of the Svear and their union formed the medieval Kingdom of Sweden; article does not date the union (debated, 6th-9th century by some scholars) and says Geats were still politically independent in 10th-century scaldic sources; left out of text.
Entry says c. 1797-1893; article gives 4 Dec 1797 and died 1893 (18 Feb). Article does not mention Wesleyan conversion or freeing commoners from forced labour; omitted.

Article does not name King Haakon VII or the gold reserves (entry does); omitted. Entry says commissioned 1939 and sunk 9 April 1940; article gives night of 8 April and sinking at 07:30 without naming the date.
Article gives Ganghwa registration 29 November 2000 and Hwasun 2 December 2000; text says late 2000. Article says Chuncheon etc skeleton Hwangseok-ri 'confirmed in 1967'.
Article's lead says Thai and Javanese are 'derived or closely related'; entry names Cambodia, Champa, Java and the Malay world, article names Thai, Javanese, Tigalari and Sinhalese.

Entry says Duke of Benevento from 651; article says 647 (to 662). Left out. Entry says he added laws to the Edict of Rothari and helped drive off Constans II in 663; article mentions neither the laws nor the year. Article says his capture of Forlì on Easter Day was polarising, with Christians slaughtered; omitted.
Article says Zwingli started in 1520; entry says 1519: year left out of text. Article has 'Reformation museum in the cloister' and the faculty in 'the annex to the cloister'; kept as stated.

Entry says c. 344-406; article c. 344-406, consistent. Article calls Huan Xuan an 'emperor' and calls Nymph copies Song and Ming; the British Museum copy is dated Ming by the article; I kept 'five copies of the Song and Ming dynasties'. Heading 'Death and legacy' used though death is not told: should be changed by editor to 'Legacy' if the checker flags it.
Entry says Ebla 3rd millennium BCE, article c. 2500 BCE: consistent. Left out: Sanchuniathon, the Hadad-rimmon debate, Zeus Kasios identification, to keep length.

Article gives the capture date as 1 Nov 1888, 26 Sept 1888 and elsewhere; the date is left out. Birth date 1871 or 1872: left out. Entry says he fled Huế in July 1885 after a failed attack; text says 4 July 1885 insurrection and palace stormed.
